title: Liquid AI LFM2.5-24B-A2B: 2B-Active MoE for On-Device AI
summary: Liquid AI launches LFM2.5-24B-A2B, a 24B MoE model with 2B active parameters. Scores 48.09 on LiveClaw, decodes 184 tokens/s on Apple M5 Max.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Liquid AI released LFM2.5-24B-A2B, a 24 billion parameter MoE model with only 2 billion active parameters for efficient on-device inference.
- The model achieves 48.09 on the LiveClaw benchmark and decodes at 184 tokens per second on Apple's M5 Max chip.
- Open-weight architecture enables local agent deployment without cloud dependencies, targeting privacy-sensitive enterprise and consumer applications.


Liquid AI has officially launched LFM2.5-24B-A2B, a 24 billion parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) reasoning model designed specifically for on-device agent applications. Officially released on October 14, 2026, the model activates only 2 billion parameters during inference, enabling rapid local deployment without cloud connectivity. Early benchmarks show the model achieving 48.09 on LiveClaw and decoding at 184 tokens per second on Apple's M5 Max chip.


## Architecture and Efficiency Design


LFM2.5-24B-A2B employs a sparse Mixture-of-Experts architecture that routes input through specialized expert networks rather than activating all 24 billion parameters simultaneously. This design reduces computational overhead by 92 percent while maintaining reasoning capabilities comparable to dense models. The 2 billion active parameter configuration fits comfortably within the memory constraints of high-end consumer hardware, making the model practical for deployment on laptops and mobile workstations.


The open-weight release allows enterprises and developers to customize the model for domain-specific agent tasks without vendor lock-in. Liquid AI has prioritized inference speed and memory efficiency, targeting use cases where low latency and data privacy requirements prohibit cloud-based processing.


## Benchmark Performance and Real-World Validation


The model's 48.09 score on the LiveClaw benchmark places it among the top-performing open-weight models for agentic reasoning tasks. LiveClaw evaluates multi-step planning, tool use, and contextual decision-making across simulated real-world scenarios. The 184 tokens per second throughput on Apple M5 Max hardware represents a significant milestone for on-device language model deployment:


- Decode speed exceeds most cloud-based APIs for short-context tasks
- Latency remains under 50 milliseconds for typical agent interactions
- Memory footprint stays below 8GB during active inference


These specifications enable responsive conversational agents and workflow automation tools that operate entirely offline. Financial services, healthcare providers, and government agencies managing sensitive data represent primary target markets for the technology.


## Release Date and Availability


Liquid AI officially launched LFM2.5-24B-A2B on October 14, 2026, with immediate availability through the company's model repository. The open-weight license permits commercial use with minimal restrictions, though Liquid AI recommends organizations implement responsible AI governance frameworks before deployment. The model weights total approximately 12 gigabytes in standard precision format, with quantized versions planned for release in Q4 2026.


Apple M5 Max optimization includes native support for the chip's unified memory architecture and neural engine acceleration. Liquid AI has indicated that compatibility updates for other ARM-based platforms and x86 systems will follow in the coming weeks.


## Implications for On-Device AI Agents


The combination of reasoning capability and hardware efficiency positions LFM2.5-24B-A2B as a practical foundation for next-generation personal and enterprise agents. Unlike cloud-dependent systems, locally-deployed models eliminate network latency, reduce operational costs, and provide absolute data privacy. Industries handling regulated information can now implement sophisticated AI assistants without transmitting sensitive data to third-party servers.


The sparse MoE architecture also demonstrates a path forward for scaling language models without proportional increases in inference cost. As consumer devices continue improving in processing power and memory capacity, models like LFM2.5-24B-A2B suggest that the performance gap between local and cloud-based AI will continue narrowing through architectural innovation rather than raw parameter scaling.


## What This Means


Liquid AI's LFM2.5-24B-A2B represents a significant step toward practical on-device AI agents that balance performance with efficiency. By activating only 2 billion of 24 billion total parameters, the model achieves competitive reasoning scores while running at speeds that make real-time interaction feasible on consumer hardware. The open-weight release lowers barriers to entry for organizations building privacy-preserving AI systems, potentially accelerating adoption in regulated industries where cloud solutions remain impractical. As hardware capabilities advance and model architectures continue optimizing for sparse computation, the boundary between local and cloud-based AI applications will increasingly blur.
